newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut says result reflects improving trend.
newsitem.headline: NatMut says result reflects improving trend.

text.p: Life insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday its A$175.5 million interim net profit to March 31 continued an improving trend at the group.
"This is a satisfying result for our 500,000 plus shareholders," managing director Geoff Tomlinson said.
The figure represented a 33.5 percent improvement on the same period last year, based on the restated profit in the share offer document, he said.
Tomlinson said shareholders had received 6.4 percent growth in value during the half from a four cent per share dividend and a seven cent per share growth in assets.

Australia and New Zealand financial services group National Mutual Life contributed A$111 million to the result. The 58 percent owned Hong Kong life insurer National Mutual Asia , which reported last week, contributed A$67 million.
National Mutual Funds Management contributed A$5 million and Australian Casualty and Life A$6 million, while National Mutual Health Insurance made a A$10 million loss.
Tomlinson said retail sales at National Mutual Life rose 45 percent compared with the same period last year and retail withdrawals were maintained at similar levels.
"As a result net cash flow in these productions improved significantly to A$400 million," he said.
However, increased competition led to lower than expected risk product sales.
Tomlinson said funds under management at National Mutual Funds Management rose 9.1 percent, largely because of favourable financial markets.
The health insurance arm, which trades as HBA in Victoria, Mutual Community in South Australia and National Mutual Health in other states, experienced difficult market conditions.
However, Tomlinson said the loss was due largely to a A$9.2 million write-down of property and hospital investments.
Australian Casualty and Life increased premiums by 8.9 percent to A$64 million.
Claims on income protection products continued to be a major issue for the business but steps had been taken to address the issue, he said.
